rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the body part, and in compounds such as 頁頭 it can mean the front or beginning of something.

example.jyutping: ngo5 go3 tau4 zung6 tung3 gan2

rows.meaning: go to the front; lead off
rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose verb for being in charge of people or leading a group or procession.

example.english: I head the volunteer team into the venue.
example.traditional: 我帶領義工隊行入會場。
example.jyutping: ngo5 daai3 ling5 ji6 gung1 deoi6 haang4 jap6 wui6 coeng4

rows.meaning: go to the front; lead off
rows.note: Use this when emphasizing that a person or group goes first or leads off at the front.

example.english: You head off first, and we’ll follow you.
example.traditional: 你帶頭行先，我哋跟住你。
example.jyutping: nei5 daai3 tau4 haang4 sin1 ngo5 dei6 gan1 zyu6 nei5

rows.note: Use this pattern when saying that someone is travelling in a particular direction, rather than merely going somewhere.

example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 hoeng3 bak1 min6 haang4

rows.note: Use 頭腦 for someone's intelligence or mental capacity, and for the mind or thoughts in expressions such as 有商業頭腦.

example.english: They have a good head for business.
example.jyutping: keoi5 hou2 jau5 saang1 ji3 tau4 nou5

rows.note: Use this specifically for striking a football with the head.

example.english: They head the ball into the net and win the match.
example.traditional: 佢哋頂波入網，贏咗場波。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 ding2 bo1 jap6 mong5 jing4 zo2 coeng4 bo1

rows.note: Use this colloquial word for the boss or person in charge, not for the broader expert sense of English “head.”

example.english: The head of my team told me to come in early tomorrow.
example.traditional: 我阿頭叫我聽日返早啲。
example.jyutping: ngo5 aa3 tau4 giu3 ngo5 ting1 jat6 faan1 zou2 di1

rows.note: Use this noun phrase when referring to one head or clump of lettuce; Cantonese normally expresses the quantity with a classifier.

example.english: I bought a head of lettuce.
example.jyutping: ngo5 maai5 zo2 jat1 fo2 saang1 coi3
